keywords.chittor: Chittorgarh Fort is the pride of Mewar, famous for Rani Padmini's courage, Vijay Stambh, and sacred Jauhar Kund.
keywords.chittorgarh: Chittorgarh stands on a 180-meter hill and endured three heroic sieges in Mewar's legendary history.
keywords.vijay stambh: Vijay Stambh is a 9-storey, 122-foot Tower of Victory built by Maharana Kumbha in 1448 AD to celebrate victory over Malwa.
keywords.tower: The Tower of Victory features 157 spiral steps with carved statues of Hindu deities on every single floor.
keywords.kumbhalgarh: Kumbhalgarh Fort boasts a 36-kilometer continuous wall, the second longest in the world after the Great Wall of China!
keywords.wall: The Great Wall of Kumbhalgarh is eight meters wide, allowing four horsemen to ride side-by-side along its ramparts.
keywords.badal mahal: Badal Mahal (Palace of Clouds) sits at the peak of Kumbhalgarh, providing cool mountain breezes and panoramic desert views.
keywords.kuldhara: Kuldhara is an abandoned desert village where 84 Paliwal Brahmin villages vanished overnight in 1825 AD.
keywords.bhangarh: Bhangarh Fort is known for Princess Ratnavati and Tantrik Singhia's legend, surrounded by 7-tiered ruined palaces.
keywords.chaupar: Chaupar is an ancient royal cross-shaped dice game played with wooden pasa dice, testing patience and strategic skill.
keywords.salim singh: Diwan Salim Singh demanded an oppressive 300% tax and threatened the chief's daughter, forcing the villagers to evacuate.
keywords.drought: Severe desert drought dried up Kuldhara's stepwells, forcing the Paliwal Brahmins to abandon their homes overnight.

spoiler_response: That you have to find out, my aaka! Search the silent ruins, inspect the three clues, and uncover the mystery yourself.
general_lore: Khamma Ghani, mere aaka! Legendary Rajputana is a land of unyielding fortresses, chivalry, and desert mysteries!
